"Role: Senior Mobile Game Developer @COMMENT_BODY@ Systems Programmer
Tech Stack: HTML5 Canvas / Phaser.js (or Unity C#) - Optimized for Android Mobile Touchscreens (No Keyboard or Mouse required).

Goal: Build a top-down pixel-art arcade action game directly inspired by Tangram Games' \"Mr. Rescue\" (image 1), adapting its side-scrolling platformer mechanics into a 2D top-down perspective with added tactical fire-type matching elements.

---

### 1. CORE VISUALS @COMMENT_BODY@ PERSPECTIVE
- Camera: Top-down 2D orthographic camera with pixel-art graphics (16-bit aesthetic, CRT scanline overlay toggle).
- Character @COMMENT_BODY@ World:
  - Playable Firefighter sprite wearing a red helmet and turnout gear.
  - Building interior with rooms, hallways, furniture, and windows (victims can be thrown out of windows or taken to building exit doors).

---

### 2. DUAL TOUCH CONTROLS @COMMENT_BODY@ UI (Android Touch Native)

1. Movement Joystick (Bottom-Left Screen): Floating 360-degree virtual joystick controlling walking movement.
2. Aim @COMMENT_BODY@ Spray Zone (Right Half Screen):
   - Touch/drag right side of the screen to aim the firefighter torso and extinguisher nozzle 360 degrees.
   - Dedicated \"SPRAY\" button: Hold to discharge the selected extinguisher.
3. Dedicated Action Buttons:
   - \"GRAB / THROW\" Button: Tap near a civilian victim to pick them up onto your shoulders. Tap again to THROW the victim toward an open window or safety door!
4. On-Screen Radial Extinguisher Wheel (Top-Right HUD Icon):
   - Tapping opens a quick-select touch wheel to swap between 4 Extinguisher Tanks:
     1. 🔴 Water Tank (Standard stream particle)
     2. 🔵 CO2 Tank (Broad cold gas cloud)
     3. 🟡 Chemical Foam Tank (Sticky foam stream)
     4. ❄️ Ice / Cryo Tank (Freezing blast stream)

---

### 3. THE 4 FIRE ENEMY TYPES @COMMENT_BODY@ EXTINGUISHER MATCHING

Fires move, spread, and act as dynamic enemies across floor tiles. Each fire type requires its matching extinguisher type:

1. 🔥 Standard Blaze (Class A / Wood @COMMENT_BODY@ Furniture):
   - Effective Tool: Water Extinguisher 🔴
   - Wrong Tool Effect: CO2 or Ice barely damages it; Chemical Foam causes low damage.
2. ⚡ Spark / Electrical Fire (Class C / Electronics @COMMENT_BODY@ Racks):
   - Effective Tool: CO2 Extinguisher 🔵
   - Wrong Tool Effect: Water on Electrical Fire creates an ELECTRIFIED FLOOD tile that damages the player!
3. 🧪 Chemical / Fuel Fire (Class B / Oil Drums @COMMENT_BODY@ Kitchens):
   - Effective Tool: Chemical Foam Extinguisher 🟡
   - Wrong Tool Effect: Water on Chemical Fire expands the fire radius into a sudden flare-up.
4. 🌋 Infernal / Magma Ember (Extreme Heat / Core Fires):
   - Effective Tool: Ice / Cryo Extinguisher ❄️
   - Wrong Tool Effect: Water evaporates instantly into blinding steam that blocks player visibility.

---

### 4. CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP (Mr. Rescue Mechanics)

1. Infiltration @COMMENT_BODY@ Heat Management:
   - A global \"Building Temperature / Overheat\" bar fills up at the top of the HUD. If the temperature hits 100%, the building collapses.
2. Rescue Victims:
   - Civilian NPCs run in panic inside rooms.
   - The player must walk up to them, hit \"GRAB\", carry them (which slightly slows player movement), and THROW them out of open windows or into green exit zones to score points and drop building temperature.
3. Extinguish @COMMENT_BODY@ Navigate:
   - Identify the fire enemy type blocking hallway routes or threatening victims.
   - Tap the radial wheel to switch to the correct Extinguisher Tank, aim, and spray to clear a path.

---

### 5. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Provide clean, modular TypeScript or HTML5 Canvas code containing:
1. Touch Input System: Multi-touch engine handling simultaneous Left Joystick, Right Aiming, Spray Hold, Grab/Throw, and Radial Menu taps.
2. Fire Grid @COMMENT_BODY@ Particle Collision Engine: Cellular automata grid managing fire spread, heat generation, and particle collision checks between extinguisher spray and specific fire enemy types.
3. Victim Physics Engine: Throwing trajectory mechanic (calculating arc velocity when throwing victims toward windows/exits).
4. HUD Overlay: Real-time temperature bar, score, victim count, and active extinguisher indicator.

Generate full, playable prototype code showcasing top-down movement, Mr. Rescue-style victim throwing, radial tank selection, and extinguisher/fire matching logic.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down pixel-art firefighter rescue game optimized for mobile touch controls, with extinguisher/fire matching, victim rescue, and a temperature-collapse loop.

## Requirements
- HTML5 Canvas/Phaser.js or Unity C#; mobile touch required, no keyboard or mouse.
- Include simultaneous movement/aim/spray/action controls, four extinguisher types with matching fire interactions, victim throwing to exits/windows, HUD, and optional CRT overlay.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save and inspect a recent small JPEG screenshot for checks.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML5 Canvas game named **HOTLINE 9**, with CSS and plain JavaScript; no dependencies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created initial canvas game shell, styling, pixel-art building map/rendering, player/fire/victim drawings, HUD, touch input handlers, radial tank menu, and portions of movement, fire, and victim logic.

### Active
- Finish and validate `game.js`; the file is currently incomplete and not playable.
- Verify controls/gameplay in a browser and capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `game.js` has no completed closing game loop/IIFE; the last edit attempted to add it but failed.
- `game.js` contains a syntax error at line 239: `ctx.fillStyle='#081012cc;ctx.fillRect...` has a missing closing quote.
- No tests or browser verification have been run.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and repair `game.js`, including the malformed title overlay line and closing `drawOverlay`, animation loop, and IIFE.
2. Run a JavaScript syntax check, then start the project using its available startup workflow and verify gameplay.
3. Fix any runtime/control issues; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game page and canvas shell.
- `style.css`: Responsive viewport, pixel rendering, CRT scanline and vignette styling.
- `game.js`: Game implementation in progress; currently syntactically incomplete.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `startup.sh`: Startup script stub.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The intended game code includes four fire classes/tanks, a cellular-style fire-spread attempt, electrified-flood/flare-up/steam reactions, survivor throwing toward exits/windows, and touch HUD controls, but these features are unverified.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down pixel-art firefighter rescue game optimized for mobile touch controls, with extinguisher/fire matching, victim rescue, and a temperature-collapse loop.

## Requirements
- Use HTML5 Canvas/Phaser.js or Unity C#; mobile touch controls required, with no keyboard or mouse dependency.
- Support simultaneous movement, aiming, spraying, grab/throw actions, four extinguisher types, HUD, and optional CRT overlay.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save and inspect a recent small JPEG screenshot for checks.

## Decisions
- Implemented as standalone HTML5 Canvas game **HOTLINE 9**, using CSS and plain JavaScript with no dependencies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and a substantial `game.js` implementation with pixel-art rendering, building layout, HUD, touch input, extinguisher wheel, fires, victims, and rescue mechanics.
- Fixed the malformed title overlay color string in `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish and validate `game.js`; add the missing completed animation loop and IIFE closure.
- Verify controls and gameplay in a browser and capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `game.js` remains incomplete: it currently ends after `drawOverlay()` without a `requestAnimationFrame` loop or closing IIFE.
- No syntax check, runtime test, browser verification, or screenshot capture has been run.

## Next Move
1. Add the animation loop and close the IIFE in `game.js`.
2. Run a JavaScript syntax check; repair any syntax or runtime issues.
3. Launch the project, verify gameplay and touch controls, then capture and inspect a recent small JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Main implementation; still needs game loop and validation.
- `index.html`: Standalone game page and canvas shell.
- `style.css`: Responsive viewport and CRT overlay styling.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `startup.sh`: Startup script stub.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The intended implementation includes four fire classes/tanks, fire spread, hazard reactions, victim throwing to exits/windows, and touch controls; these features are unverified.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
